version.changelog:
No user-facing changes detected in this version.

- No file changes were detected.
- Behavior and documentation remain unchanged from the previous version.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed browser automation tool, but it exposes broad local code execution and file-writing through a persistent localhost daemon, so it belongs in Review rather than automatic install.

dimensions.detail: The requested Bash node, pw-browser, and curl authority is coherent with browser automation, but the resulting tool can navigate arbitrary sites, submit forms, modify live web content, read browser storage through page code, and write files when invoked.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal npm-based Playwright dependency with no package scripts observed, but package.json uses a caret range for Playwright and no lockfile was present in the inspected artifact set.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation warns that run-code/eval are for trusted local use and should not run unknown code, but the daemon interface itself does not enforce authentication, allowlisting, or per-call user approval.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon persists across commands on 127.0.0.1:19223 and writes state under ~/.pw-browser; it can be closed, but while active it exposes powerful actions over a local HTTP interface and accepts unrestricted screenshot output paths.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Most capabilities fit Playwright browser automation, but run-code executes arbitrary daemon-side Node/Playwright code and eval executes arbitrary page scripts, expanding the skill from browser control into high-impact host execution.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a trusted local environment. Do not expose the daemon as a service, do not leave it running unnecessarily, avoid running code snippets from webpages or third parties, and prefer closing it with pw-browser close --all after use. Review the unrestricted run-code/eval and screenshot path behavior before using it with sensitive accounts or business systems.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The front matter is brief, but the SKILL.md body prominently documents the daemon, run-code/eval, disk-write implications, and local-trust limits, so this is a metadata-disclosure gap rather than hidden behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: Dynamic page and Playwright code is an advanced browser-automation capability and is documented, but it is high-impact and depends on trusted local use.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact implements run-code with new Function in the daemon process, which creates host-side execution beyond ordinary fixed browser actions and is a main reason for Review.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Screenshots are expected for browser automation, but accepting an unrestricted custom path is broader than necessary and can overwrite files writable by the daemon user.
[SQP-2] expected: The no-warning framing is not fully supported because the skill includes explicit warnings for run-code/eval, but the execution primitive remains materially risky.
[SC1] expected: A Playwright dependency is expected, while the caret range and absent lockfile are supply-chain hygiene concerns rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SC4] expected: The artifact declares Playwright with a caret range starting at 1.51.0, so dependency upgrade and pinning guidance is relevant, but the exact installed version is not fixed by the artifact alone.
